questions: Did slalom line_loss_events fall from 1.0 to 0 with the 20 mm pitch?
Did s-bend progress rise above 0.04 with wheel_track 0.10 m and mass 0.6 kg, and did max_error stay below 0.06 m?
Did any track complete? If not, which track ended off track first, and at what progress?
Did steering_oscillation rise above 0.16 on any track? If so, the next step is the sensor y offset of 0.05 m.
Does mass 0.6 kg cause any wheel slip or unstable turning on the slalom?
feedback_request.what_to_report: Per track (oval, s-bend, slalom): completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, controller_errors. Also the kp that gave the best rms_error with this layout, and which sensors carry most signal on the line.

intent: Test whether a wider 20 mm pitch (x = ±0.06 m) removes the slalom line loss left by the contiguous 16 mm layout, and whether a narrower wheel track (0.10 m) with lower mass (0.6 kg) raises turn rate enough to stop the s-bend drift. Expect line_loss_events of 0 on the slalom, s-bend progress above 0.04, and a first completion on at least one development track.
learning: Iteration 3 repeated iteration 2's geometry with kp 5.0 and returned identical metrics, so gain alone does not change the s-bend result. Iteration 4 changes sensor pitch and drivetrain together. The s-bend result is the cleanest read of the drivetrain change, because that track has no line loss to confound it. If the s-bend stays at 0.04 progress, the next lever is wheel_track 0.08 m, or a lower mass near 0.4 kg, rather than more sensors.
rationale: Iteration 2 (16 mm contiguous sensors, x = ±0.048 m) removed line loss on the oval and s-bend, which supports the footprint fix. Two problems remain. First, the slalom still loses the line once per run (line_loss_events 1.0, max_error 0.0628 m), so the 4 to 5 cm error zone is not fully covered. The Integrator's pre-agreed rule applies: widen the pitch to 20 mm (x = -0.06 to +0.06 m, y = 0.03 m). Second, the s-bend has zero line loss but progress of only 0.04 with max_error 0.0611 m, so the robot leaves the tape through turn-rate lag, not lost sensing. Iteration 3 repeated iteration 2's geometry and returned identical metrics to four decimals, so the kp change had no visible effect and the s-bend failure is not a gain problem. Steering oscillation is 0.075 on the oval and 0.14 on the slalom, both below the 0.16 threshold, so I leave the sensor y offset at 0.03 m. For turn rate, I reduce wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m, which raises the turn rate per unit wheel differential by about 20 percent, and reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia, as the Integrator's fallback suggests. The s-bend should barely depend on the sensor pitch change, since it has no line loss, so any s-bend progress gain can be credited mostly to the drivetrain change. The slalom result will mix both changes, so I treat it as a combined test. I keep body width 0.12 m and body length 0.16 m because the off-track limit is 0.06 m for any allowed width. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events near zero, s-bend progress above 0.04, and a first completion on the oval or s-bend. Watch for slip at lower mass.
